retention: Bind Task still executes the same Runtime coroutine; its frame self retains Runtime until that coroutine finishes, including cleanup on failed validation. The transient callback local also retains Runtime through each acquisition, replacing the former Runtime select frame self. A cached selection still drops this local when acquisition returns.

Release Task still executes the Runtime finish-use coroutine, retaining Runtime through locked decrement and the physical release. The moved shield loop holds its transient finish_use callback through the same task/result/cancellation handling interval previously held by its Runtime self. Nothing is stored in the long-lived lease owner.

Configuration partial retains Runtime/candidates only while the existing Runtime commit call is active; owner does not persist it. No permanent Runtime -> leases -> stored callback -> Runtime cycle is introduced. The original Task-mediated transient Runtime retention now passes through the lease owner Task map and ends at the same task/waiter cleanup boundary.
unacceptable_shortcuts: Move bind/release Task coroutine receiver to leases and claim lifetime unchanged.
Store Runtime/bound callbacks in the lease owner.
Expose a raw lock/map or implement a private mixin/property.
Create a second configuration lock or strengthen commit guard with the desired-fingerprint map.

accounting.retention: Each provider now holds three needed bound Runtime I/O methods instead of the _runtime field. Their __self__ is the same Runtime. They are assigned and retained for the provider lifetime; renew_delegate does not replace/clear them. This preserves the provider -> Runtime strong edge until provider retirement. Runtime does not store these callbacks or a journal object containing them, so no new permanent cycle is formed. The callbacks are used for actual existing I/O, not inert keepalive state.
accounting.late_lookup: Each callback resolves self.conversation_storage_services.event_store and its concrete method at the original I/O execution point. Capturing an EventStore or its bound read/append method at provider construction would freeze the former late lookup and would not itself retain Runtime; reject that shortcut.
accounting.patch_boundary: Existing Runtime private helper patches must move mechanically to the true journal public function owner, using qualified journal module calls so the provider and Runtime workflow share that patch boundary. Tests/test_specialist_orchestration.py:667,677,740,750,777 patch validation publication and are concrete witnesses for preserving the retry/publication boundary. This proposal intentionally changes helper owner paths; it does not promise old Runtime/private/subclass dispatch after the allowed owner migration.
accounting.no_new_behavior: Read/append counts, batch/UUID/deterministic digest creation, exception text/priority, event ordering, await positions and existing receipt/tuple/projection identities stay unchanged. No new lock, Task, DTO, store, storage scope, flush, queue or I/O.
